```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(reproducible.verbose = -1)
```

A project often reads data from many places: files on the web, Google Drive, other people's
folders. Sooner or later someone asks "what does this project need?": to cite the data, to
check a source has not changed, or to run the project on a machine with no internet.

reproducible answers that question with a *download ledger*. Every call to `prepInputs()` or
`preProcess()` writes one record: the address, the file it was meant to give, and where it was
put. A call with no `url` that reads a file already on disk is recorded too, with
`local:<path>` in place of the address. This vignette shows how to read the ledger, how it behaves with `Cache()`, and
how to go from the ledger to the list of files to copy to another machine.

# The ledger of a session

`prepInputsLog()` returns every access of the current R session. `clearUrlLog()` empties it.
The examples here use local files given as `file://` urls, so they run without internet; a
`https://` or Google Drive url is recorded the same way.

```{r ledger}
library(reproducible)
src <- file.path(tempdir(), "sources")
dir.create(src, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines("a,b\n1,2", file.path(src, "table.csv"))
writeLines("x,y\n3,4", file.path(src, "other.csv"))
url1 <- paste0("file://", file.path(src, "table.csv"))
url2 <- paste0("file://", file.path(src, "other.csv"))
inputs <- file.path(tempdir(), "inputs")

clearUrlLog()
tab <- prepInputs(url = url1, targetFile = "table.csv", destinationPath = inputs, fun = NA)

data.table::rbindlist(prepInputsLog(), fill = TRUE)[, c("fn", "url", "targetFile", "destinationPath")]
```

A url is recorded when it is used, whether or not a download was needed: the second time the
file is already in `destinationPath`, but the project still uses it.

A file read with no `url` is recorded as `local:` and its path. These are inputs someone put
on the disk by hand; they have no source to download from, so they must be copied.

```{r local}
writeLines("id\n1", file.path(inputs, "byHand.csv"))
clearUrlLog()
byHand <- prepInputs(targetFile = "byHand.csv", destinationPath = inputs, fun = NA)
led <- data.table::rbindlist(prepInputsLog(), fill = TRUE)
led[, c("fn", "url")]
led[!startsWith(url, "local:")] # only the remote sources
```

# The ledger and `Cache()`

On a cache hit the cached function does not run, so nothing is downloaded. The ledger would miss
the data if it relied on the download. Instead, `Cache()` stores the urls read inside it as tags
on the cache entry, and replays them on every hit. The ledger of a run is therefore the same
whether its steps were computed or came from the cache.

```{r cache}
options(reproducible.cachePath = file.path(tempdir(), "cache"))
getTables <- function(u1, u2, dp) {
  list(prepInputs(url = u1, targetFile = "table.csv", destinationPath = dp, fun = NA),
       prepInputs(url = u2, targetFile = "other.csv", destinationPath = dp, fun = NA))
}

clearUrlLog()
out <- Cache(getTables(url1, url2, inputs)) # computed
clearUrlLog()
out <- Cache(getTables(url1, url2, inputs)) # a cache hit: nothing runs, the urls are replayed
data.table::rbindlist(prepInputsLog(), fill = TRUE)[, c("fn", "url", "targetFile", "cacheId")]
```

This holds for nested calls too. If an outer `Cache()` is computed and an inner `Cache()` inside
it is a hit, the inner urls are passed to the outer entry, so a later hit of the outer entry
replays them.

The tags stay in the cache after the session ends. `urlLog()` reads them for a whole cache
folder: the data every cached step of a project has used.

```{r urlLog}
urlLog(getOption("reproducible.cachePath"),
       which = c("function", "url", "targetFile", "destinationPath"))
```

# In a SpaDES project

SpaDES.core keeps one ledger per run: `urlLog(sim)` gives the records of that `simList`, with the
module and event that read each url. The records also reach `prepInputsLog()`. Event caching,
`.inputObjects` caching and `cacheChaining` all replay the tags, as above.

```{r spades, eval = FALSE}
sim <- SpaDES.core::simInitAndSpades(...)
urlLog(sim, which = c("module", "event", "url", "targetFile", "destinationPath"))
```

# Data read by other means

The ledger only sees `prepInputs()` and `preProcess()` (and `CacheGeo()`). Code that downloads
with `download.file()`, `googledrive::drive_download()` or a web-service package should say so
with `logUrlAccess()`, once per access, just before the download. Inside `Cache()` it is tagged
and replayed like any other record.

```{r other}
getStation <- function(id) {
  u <- paste0("https://example.com/stations/", id, ".csv")
  logUrlAccess(u, targetFile = paste0(id, ".csv"))
  # download.file(u, ...) would go here
  data.frame(id = id)
}
clearUrlLog()
st <- getStation("A1")
data.table::rbindlist(prepInputsLog(), fill = TRUE)[, c("fn", "url")]
```

`?prepInputsLog` lists everything that is recorded and the few cases that are not (for example a
cache entry made with `options(reproducible.urlLog = FALSE)`).

# Running a project without internet

To run a project on a machine without internet, copy the files it reads. Two tools give that list,
and they answer different questions.

1. **The ledger** names every input `prepInputs()` read: each url with the `destinationPath` and
   `targetFile` it was saved as, and each local file (`local:<path>`). Copy those files (and
   `archive`, if one was given) into the same `destinationPath` on the other machine, and
   `prepInputs()` finds them there without downloading. This list is complete even when the run came from the cache, because hits replay
   their urls.

    ```{r copyList}
    ## from the cache; for one session, data.table::rbindlist(prepInputsLog(), fill = TRUE)
    led <- urlLog(getOption("reproducible.cachePath"),
                  which = c("url", "targetFile", "destinationPath"))
    led <- led[!is.na(targetFile) & !is.na(destinationPath)]
    unique(file.path(led$destinationPath, led$targetFile))
    ```

2. **`filesUsedTrace()`** (Linux, needs `strace`) runs a script and returns every existing file
   under the given folders that the run opened: inputs, cache entries, module code. It shows
   exactly what *this* run read, but no more. On a cache hit the raw inputs behind the entry are
   never opened, so they are not in the list. If the cache key then changes on the other machine,
   the step is recomputed and needs those raw inputs.

    ```{r trace, eval = FALSE}
    used <- filesUsedTrace("run.R", folders = c("inputs", "cache"))
    ```

For a machine without internet, copy both: the traced files (cache entries and anything read
locally), and the files the ledger names (the raw inputs, so a cache miss there can still be
recomputed). Or copy the project's whole input and cache folders, if they are not too large.
